actions.action: Enforce creation and opening eligibility server-side
actions.mechanism: Creation requires the flag and format-write capability; opening requires format-read capability, independently of the creation flag.
actions.implementation: Check authorization and capabilities on every request. Bind capability caches to client installation and declaration revision, never account alone; require fresh declaration for new-format operations.
actions.check: Seed a capable cache entry, then request through an old client on the same account; verify no new-format payload is delivered.
actions.risk: Declared capabilities cannot prove parser correctness.

actions.action: Fork incompatible changes instead of replacing legacy documents
actions.mechanism: Separate document identities preserve old clients’ existing access without translating unsupported content.
actions.implementation: Keep existing documents in their original format. Put incompatible edits in explicitly linked new-format forks; retain legacy permissions and clearly label divergence for new clients.
actions.check: Have old and new clients edit concurrently: the old client still reads the legacy document; incompatible fork content never enters it.
actions.risk: Branches diverge; merging requires explicit compatibility checks.

actions.action: Make rollback disable creation, not existing-document access
actions.mechanism: Separate creation enablement from durable format support so rollback cannot strand or destroy stored documents.
actions.implementation: Retain compatible readers, storage, and export paths during rollback. Reject new-format creation and freeze existing new-format writes explicitly; never delete or down-convert them.
actions.check: Create a new-format document, roll back, then verify capable clients can reopen it unchanged, creation fails, and legacy reads still succeed.
actions.risk: Reader services must outlive the rollout flag.
